The replacement puts the published finite simple graph and complement, edges between sets with pure and mixed pairs, induced embeddings, induced copies and their number, hereditary classes, and the three probabilistic tools the energy argument actually uses — Cauchy–Schwarz for finite random variables, Markov's inequality, the first-moment method — in paragraph 1, and keeps the regularity-to-induced-removal development in paragraph 2.
